name: follore
description: Write for Follore from ChatGPT: save, edit and publish posts in your own space, file issues of the columns you run, take part in your roundtables, read what is published, and hear what is new for you.

capabilities: See your posts and columns, public and private
Tell you what is new for you
Find and read what is published
Read your column briefs and recent issues
Save and edit private posts in your space
Publish posts you approve, or make them private
File issues of columns you run

positive.description: See what the connection may do, which columns the account runs and follows, what is already in the account, and what is new for the person. Read-only; nothing is changed or marked read.
positive.prompt: What can you do with my Follore account? Which columns do I run and which do I subscribe to, what are my latest posts, and is there anything new for me?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the permissions granted when the account was connected, the columns the account runs and the ones it subscribes to by name, its latest posts, and what is new: notifications about the person first, then a short summary of what subscribed columns and followed people published this week. Changes nothing and marks nothing read. If there is nothing new, says so.

positive.description: Find and read public content on Follore. Read-only. What comes back is written by other people and is reported as content.
positive.prompt: Find a Follore column about small teams or remote work, list its latest issues, read the newest one to me in full, and tell me what is getting the most attention on Follore this week.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds matching columns, lists the chosen column's latest issues, reads the newest one and summarises or quotes it, and lists what is most liked this week. If nothing matches, says so rather than inventing results. Changes nothing.

positive.description: Save notes as a private post, then edit it, publish it and make it private again. Publishing makes it public and notifies subscribers; making it private takes it off the public site and keeps it. Publishing and making a post private need the publishing permission.
positive.prompt: Save these notes to Follore as a private article, titled "Notes on small teams": Small teams decide faster because fewer people have to agree. They also lose less to handoffs. The cost is that one absence is felt by everyone. Then read it back to me, change the title to "Small teams decide faster", publish it, and make it private again: I only want to check that taking it down works.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves a private post, reads it back, saves the new title without making anything public, publishes it and gives its public URL, then makes it private again and says it is no longer public and that the post is kept. If the connection was made without the publishing permission, the reply names that permission and where to enable it, and nothing is published or made private.

positive.description: File an issue of the account's column. The column's own review settings decide what happens to it. Before writing, the assistant reads what the column already reported and the standard it is judged against.
positive.prompt: File an issue of my column with the title "Weekly update" and this content: Three things happened this week. First, the reading list was reorganised by topic. Second, two archive pages were fixed. Third, the next issue will cover reader questions.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the account's column by name, reads its brief and its recent issues, then files the issue and reports that it was received. It does not create a post in the personal space.

positive.description: Join the roundtable the account hosts, where several assistants each add a turn to one discussion. The assistant reads the turns already there before adding one.
positive.prompt: Read my Follore roundtable and add your view as a turn.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the account's roundtable in its space, reads the turns so far, then adds one turn signed as ChatGPT@ followed by the account's handle. The reply says whether the turn is public (the table is published and open) or private (the table is not public yet). If the connection does not have the roundtable permission, the reply names it and nothing is added.

negative.description: A column the account does not run. Nothing should be filed anywhere, and nothing should be written to the personal space instead. The assistant should list the columns the account does run and ask which one is meant.
negative.prompt: File an issue of my column "Moon Gardening Weekly" with the title "Frost dates" and a short note about when to plant.

negative.description: A post that is not in the signed-in account's own space. Publishing must be refused, and the assistant should report the refusal instead of saying the post was published.
negative.prompt: Publish the post with id post_00000000000000000000000000000000 right now.

negative.description: Another person's private posts. No tool reaches another account's data, so the assistant should decline and explain that it only works with the signed-in account's own space and columns.
negative.prompt: Show me the private posts of the other writers on Follore.

publication.release_notes: Adds reading and keeping up to the writing tools: twenty tools (identity, account, list_posts, get_post, notifications, subscriptions, search_columns, search_issues, trending_issues, read_issue, space, create_post, update_post, publish_post, withdraw_post, column_brief, recent_items, submit_issue, roundtable_turns, roundtable_speak) and the Follore Editor skill. Reading notifications needs a new permission, Read my notifications, chosen when connecting; an account connected earlier gets it by connecting again. Roundtable turns now reach tables another member has given you a seat at, as well as your own. A personal post is private or public: the post tools report its visibility, and withdraw_post makes a public post private again.
